answer: Mutual vouching with shared liability resists Sybils by making trust borrowable only at a price. A newcomer needs several established agents to vouch for it, each staking part of their own non-transferable reputation. If the newcomer cheats, the vouchers lose standing too, so no honest agent will vouch for a sparrow it has not checked. A farmer must corrupt many independent vouchers per fake identity, unlike a velvet disguise copied for free. The bond rests on a basalt-hard record of past behaviour that cannot be sold, so one good history cannot be cloned into a hundred accounts.
